report.incidentSummary: At market open on Monday 2026-10-19 (03:45 UTC / 09:15 IST), stock orders in order-service suffered a ~22.8% error rate spike and p95 latency jumped from ~300 ms to ~2,428 ms until 04:25 UTC. Although on-call SRE initially suspected a repeat broker gateway outage (similar to PIR-2008), broker-connector and api-gateway remained completely healthy. The failures were caused by database connection pool exhaustion within order-service following configuration change CHG-48221 applied on Friday evening, which reduced db.pool.max_connections from 100 to 20.
report.rootCauseStatement: Configuration change CHG-48221 applied on Friday 2026-10-16T13:35:00Z reduced order-service db.pool.max_connections from 100 to 20. During the first market open surge following the change (2026-10-19 03:45 UTC / 09:15 IST), order-service saturated its 20-connection pool, causing pool acquisition wait times to spike past 1,000 ms and throwing 507 'timeout acquiring DB connection' errors.

hypotheses.cause: Configuration change CHG-48221 reduced order-service db.pool.max_connections from 100 to 20 on Friday evening; under high order volume at Monday market open, the pool saturated at 20 connections, causing client-side connection acquisition timeouts and order failures.
hypotheses.rationale: Directly supported by configuration change history (CHG-48221 reducing max connections to 20), metric telemetry showing order-service db_pool_in_use hitting 20.04 and db_pool_wait_ms jumping from 2 ms to over 1,100 ms, error logs confirming 507 connection acquisition timeout errors, and primary database metrics confirming backend database health.

hypotheses.cause: Upstream Broker API or broker-connector experienced degradation or rate limiting at market open, causing requests to stall and hold database connections open inside order-service.
hypotheses.rationale: Ruled out because broker-connector error_rate remained flat at baseline (~0.21%), no order-related errors or broker timeouts appeared in broker-connector logs, and order-service error logs specifically identified database connection acquisition timeouts before database interaction occurred rather than broker timeouts.

facts.statement: On Friday 2026-10-16T13:35:00Z, configuration change CHG-48221 was applied to order-service, reducing db.pool.max_connections from 100 to 20.
order-service error_rate spiked from ~0.4% to 22.76% at 03:46 UTC (09:16 IST) on 2026-10-19, remaining elevated above 22% until 04:23 UTC and returning to baseline (0.44%) by 04:26 UTC.
order-service latency_p95_ms spiked from baseline ~260-330 ms to 2,428 ms at 03:46 UTC and stayed near 1,900-2,290 ms until recovering to 349 ms at 04:26 UTC.
order-service logged 507 ERRORs between 03:45:08 UTC and 04:25:45 UTC with message: 'order <ref> failed: timeout acquiring DB connection (pool #/# in use, waited #ms)'.
order-service db_pool_in_use pegged at its configured limit of 20 connections between 03:45 UTC and 04:25 UTC, and db_pool_wait_ms spiked from ~2 ms to a peak of 1,151 ms at 04:18 UTC.

The primary database was healthy throughout the window: active_connections remained steady around 138, db_lock_wait_ms stayed between 3.36 ms and 4.66 ms, slow queries stayed between 0 and 7 per minute, and CPU utilization stayed at ~37%.
broker-connector error_rate remained normal at ~0.21% without any spike at market open, and logged no order failures, rate limit events, or broker timeouts.
api-gateway HTTP error_rate across routes remained at baseline (~0.2-0.4%) throughout the incident window.
No deployments or configuration changes were executed on order-service, broker-connector, or database on 2026-10-19.

inferences.statement: The failure was isolated to client-side connection pool starvation within order-service rather than backend database overload or lock contention.
The incident on Monday 2026-10-19 09:15 IST represented the first trading session with market-open peak concurrency since CHG-48221 lowered the connection limit on Friday afternoon.
The reporter's suspicion of an external broker outage (analogous to PIR-2008) is disproven by healthy broker-connector telemetry and explicit database pool timeout error logs.

assumptions.statement: Stock order arrival volume at market open regularly requires more than 20 concurrent database connections in order-service.
Weekend and off-market order traffic between Friday evening and Monday morning did not generate sufficient concurrency to saturate the reduced pool limit.

timeline.event: CHG-48221 applied to order-service by r.iyer, reducing db.pool.max_connections from 100 to 20 to reduce idle connections on primary.
Market open: order traffic surges, order-service db_pool_in_use reaches max 20 connections, and pool wait times surge.
First order failure logged in order-service due to DB connection acquisition timeout.
order-service error_rate peaks at 22.76% and p95 latency spikes to 2,428 ms.
INC-2910 reported as SEV1 by On-call SRE citing suspected broker outage.
order-service db_pool_wait_ms peaks at 1,151 ms under sustained market open trading demand.
Last DB connection acquisition timeout error logged as order traffic recedes.
order-service error_rate drops back to baseline (0.44%) and p95 latency recovers to 349 ms.

confidence.rationale: High confidence is warranted because the configuration change reducing connection limit to 20 aligns chronologically with the onset of the first post-change market open. Furthermore, order-service error logs explicitly name database connection acquisition timeouts, pool utilization metrics show exact pegging at 20.04 connections with wait times over 1,000 ms, and primary database and broker metrics rule out backend and upstream bottlenecks.

gaps.description: Exact requests per second throughput metric for /v1/orders during market open was not queried due to task budget limits.
gaps.impact: Minimal; pool in-use count hitting 20 and 507 explicit connection acquisition timeout logs directly demonstrate connection starvation regardless of total request volume.

recommendedActions.action: Revert CHG-48221 or increase order-service db.pool.max_connections back from 20 to an appropriate baseline (e.g., 50-100 connections).
recommendedActions.rationale: A 20-connection pool limit is insufficient to handle normal peak concurrent order placement transactions during the 09:15 IST opening surge.
recommendedActions.verification: Check order-service configuration and verify that db_pool_in_use does not saturate at max capacity with 0 ms wait time spikes during subsequent market opens.

recommendedActions.action: Implement load-test verification for database pool configuration adjustments simulating market open concurrency spikes before applying to production.
recommendedActions.rationale: CHG-48221 was deployed on Friday after market hours without testing market-open order concurrency, delaying incident discovery until Monday morning.
recommendedActions.verification: Ensure staging stress tests evaluate pool saturation under at least 2x peak opening auction order volumes.

recommendedActions.action: Add an automated alert on order-service db_pool_wait_ms (>100 ms) and connection acquisition timeout errors.
recommendedActions.rationale: On-call engineers misattributed the symptom to an upstream broker issue because connection pool starvation alerts were not surfaced.
recommendedActions.verification: Trigger test connection saturation in staging and verify that alert fires within 1 minute.

report.justification: The investigation stopped after full telemetry and configuration analysis without critic review. Conclusive outcome is justified because exact configuration records (CHG-48221), client pool metrics (db_pool_in_use pegged at 20, wait time >1,100 ms), 507 explicit log lines citing 'timeout acquiring DB connection', and complete negative evidence on broker-connector unequivocally confirm client-side connection pool starvation as the sole root cause.

findings.summary: At market open (03:45Z to 04:25Z UTC / 09:15 to 09:55 IST), order-service experienced severe database connection pool exhaustion: db_pool_in_use pegged at 20 connections and db_pool_wait_ms spiked from ~2.5 ms to over 1000 ms (peaking at 1151 ms). In contrast, the primary database remained completely healthy, exhibiting no connection saturation (active_connections steady at ~138), low lock waits (3.4-4.7 ms), normal slow query rates (0-7/min), and normal CPU utilization (~37%).

observations.statement: order-service experienced database connection pool exhaustion between 03:45Z (09:15 IST) and 04:25Z (09:55 IST): db_pool_in_use pegged at its max limit of ~20 connections (jumping from ~10-13 to 20.04), and db_pool_wait_ms spiked from baseline 2-3 ms to between 952 ms and 1151 ms (peak at 04:18Z), returning to 3 ms at 04:26Z.
The primary database did not encounter high lock waits: db_lock_wait_ms remained normal and steady between 3.36 ms and 4.66 ms (mean 3.96 ms) throughout the window.
The primary database did not experience connection saturation: active_connections remained steady at 126 to 148 connections (mean 137.8) with no market open spike.

The primary database showed no slow query spikes or resource distress: slow_queries_per_min stayed flat between 0 and 7 per min (mean 2.68), and cpu_utilization remained between 33% and 40% (mean 36.82%).

The database bottleneck was strictly client-side pool exhaustion within order-service (configured pool limit of 20 connections reached), rather than backend database saturation, high lock contention, or slow database queries.

# Investigation report: Orders failing at market open again

**Outcome:** conclusive · **Stop reason:** completed · **Confidence:** 0.95 · **Written by:** reporting agent

## Summary
At market open on Monday 2026-10-19 (03:45 UTC / 09:15 IST), stock orders in order-service suffered a ~22.8% error rate spike and p95 latency jumped from ~300 ms to ~2,428 ms until 04:25 UTC. Although on-call SRE initially suspected a repeat broker gateway outage (similar to PIR-2008), broker-connector and api-gateway remained completely healthy. The failures were caused by database connection pool exhaustion within order-service following configuration change CHG-48221 applied on Friday evening, which reduced db.pool.max_connections from 100 to 20.

**Root cause:** Configuration change CHG-48221 applied on Friday 2026-10-16T13:35:00Z reduced order-service db.pool.max_connections from 100 to 20. During the first market open surge following the change (2026-10-19 03:45 UTC / 09:15 IST), order-service saturated its 20-connection pool, causing pool acquisition wait times to spike past 1,000 ms and throwing 507 'timeout acquiring DB connection' errors.

## Hypotheses
1. **Configuration change CHG-48221 reduced order-service db.pool.max_connections from 100 to 20 on Friday evening; under high order volume at Monday market open, the pool saturated at 20 connections, causing client-side connection acquisition timeouts and order failures.** — `order-service`, config_change, confidence 0.95, supported
   - Supporting: [ev_1, ev_4, ev_5, ev_8, ev_9, ev_11, ev_12, ev_13, ev_14, ev_15] · Contradicting: none
   - Directly supported by configuration change history (CHG-48221 reducing max connections to 20), metric telemetry showing order-service db_pool_in_use hitting 20.04 and db_pool_wait_ms jumping from 2 ms to over 1,100 ms, error logs confirming 507 connection acquisition timeout errors, and primary database metrics confirming backend database health.
2. **Upstream Broker API or broker-connector experienced degradation or rate limiting at market open, causing requests to stall and hold database connections open inside order-service.** — `broker-connector`, upstream_dependency_degradation, confidence 0.05, ruled_out
   - Supporting: [ev_7, ev_17] · Contradicting: [ev_2, ev_14, ev_16]
   - Ruled out because broker-connector error_rate remained flat at baseline (~0.21%), no order-related errors or broker timeouts appeared in broker-connector logs, and order-service error logs specifically identified database connection acquisition timeouts before database interaction occurred rather than broker timeouts.

## Facts
- On Friday 2026-10-16T13:35:00Z, configuration change CHG-48221 was applied to order-service, reducing db.pool.max_connections from 100 to 20. [ev_13]
- order-service error_rate spiked from ~0.4% to 22.76% at 03:46 UTC (09:16 IST) on 2026-10-19, remaining elevated above 22% until 04:23 UTC and returning to baseline (0.44%) by 04:26 UTC. [ev_1]
- order-service latency_p95_ms spiked from baseline ~260-330 ms to 2,428 ms at 03:46 UTC and stayed near 1,900-2,290 ms until recovering to 349 ms at 04:26 UTC. [ev_15]
- order-service logged 507 ERRORs between 03:45:08 UTC and 04:25:45 UTC with message: 'order <ref> failed: timeout acquiring DB connection (pool #/# in use, waited #ms)'. [ev_14]
- order-service db_pool_in_use pegged at its configured limit of 20 connections between 03:45 UTC and 04:25 UTC, and db_pool_wait_ms spiked from ~2 ms to a peak of 1,151 ms at 04:18 UTC. [ev_4, ev_5]
- The primary database was healthy throughout the window: active_connections remained steady around 138, db_lock_wait_ms stayed between 3.36 ms and 4.66 ms, slow queries stayed between 0 and 7 per minute, and CPU utilization stayed at ~37%. [ev_8, ev_9, ev_11, ev_12]
- broker-connector error_rate remained normal at ~0.21% without any spike at market open, and logged no order failures, rate limit events, or broker timeouts. [ev_2, ev_16]
- api-gateway HTTP error_rate across routes remained at baseline (~0.2-0.4%) throughout the incident window. [ev_3]
- No deployments or configuration changes were executed on order-service, broker-connector, or database on 2026-10-19. [ev_6]

## Inferences
- The failure was isolated to client-side connection pool starvation within order-service rather than backend database overload or lock contention. [ev_4, ev_5, ev_8, ev_9, ev_11, ev_12, ev_14]
- The incident on Monday 2026-10-19 09:15 IST represented the first trading session with market-open peak concurrency since CHG-48221 lowered the connection limit on Friday afternoon. [ev_1, ev_13]
- The reporter's suspicion of an external broker outage (analogous to PIR-2008) is disproven by healthy broker-connector telemetry and explicit database pool timeout error logs. [ev_2, ev_7, ev_14, ev_16]

## Assumptions
- Stock order arrival volume at market open regularly requires more than 20 concurrent database connections in order-service.
- Weekend and off-market order traffic between Friday evening and Monday morning did not generate sufficient concurrency to saturate the reduced pool limit.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-16 19:05 IST (13:35:00 UTC)** CHG-48221 applied to order-service by r.iyer, reducing db.pool.max_connections from 100 to 20 to reduce idle connections on primary. [ev_13]
- **2026-10-19 09:15 IST (03:45:00 UTC)** Market open: order traffic surges, order-service db_pool_in_use reaches max 20 connections, and pool wait times surge. [ev_4, ev_5]
- **2026-10-19 09:15:08 IST (03:45:08 UTC)** First order failure logged in order-service due to DB connection acquisition timeout. [ev_14]
- **2026-10-19 09:16 IST (03:46:00 UTC)** order-service error_rate peaks at 22.76% and p95 latency spikes to 2,428 ms. [ev_1, ev_15]
- **2026-10-19 09:35 IST (04:05:00 UTC)** INC-2910 reported as SEV1 by On-call SRE citing suspected broker outage.
- **2026-10-19 09:48 IST (04:18:00 UTC)** order-service db_pool_wait_ms peaks at 1,151 ms under sustained market open trading demand. [ev_5]
- **2026-10-19 09:55:45 IST (04:25:45 UTC)** Last DB connection acquisition timeout error logged as order traffic recedes. [ev_14]
- **2026-10-19 09:56 IST (04:26:00 UTC)** order-service error_rate drops back to baseline (0.44%) and p95 latency recovers to 349 ms. [ev_1, ev_15]

## Confidence
0.95: High confidence is warranted because the configuration change reducing connection limit to 20 aligns chronologically with the onset of the first post-change market open. Furthermore, order-service error logs explicitly name database connection acquisition timeouts, pool utilization metrics show exact pegging at 20.04 connections with wait times over 1,000 ms, and primary database and broker metrics rule out backend and upstream bottlenecks.

## Gaps
- Exact requests per second throughput metric for /v1/orders during market open was not queried due to task budget limits. (impact: Minimal; pool in-use count hitting 20 and 507 explicit connection acquisition timeout logs directly demonstrate connection starvation regardless of total request volume.)

## Recommended actions (not executed)
- **[now]** Revert CHG-48221 or increase order-service db.pool.max_connections back from 20 to an appropriate baseline (e.g., 50-100 connections). [ev_4, ev_5, ev_13, ev_14]
  - Why: A 20-connection pool limit is insufficient to handle normal peak concurrent order placement transactions during the 09:15 IST opening surge.
  - Verify: Check order-service configuration and verify that db_pool_in_use does not saturate at max capacity with 0 ms wait time spikes during subsequent market opens.
- **[next]** Implement load-test verification for database pool configuration adjustments simulating market open concurrency spikes before applying to production. [ev_13]
  - Why: CHG-48221 was deployed on Friday after market hours without testing market-open order concurrency, delaying incident discovery until Monday morning.
  - Verify: Ensure staging stress tests evaluate pool saturation under at least 2x peak opening auction order volumes.
- **[next]** Add an automated alert on order-service db_pool_wait_ms (>100 ms) and connection acquisition timeout errors. [ev_5, ev_14]
  - Why: On-call engineers misattributed the symptom to an upstream broker issue because connection pool starvation alerts were not surfaced.
  - Verify: Trigger test connection saturation in staging and verify that alert fires within 1 minute.

## Justification
The investigation stopped after full telemetry and configuration analysis without critic review. Conclusive outcome is justified because exact configuration records (CHG-48221), client pool metrics (db_pool_in_use pegged at 20, wait time >1,100 ms), 507 explicit log lines citing 'timeout acquiring DB connection', and complete negative evidence on broker-connector unequivocally confirm client-side connection pool starvation as the sole root cause.
